availability.note: GWM AU offers page prices the Cannon Alpha Lux PHEV (VIC private drive-away, as of 1/11/2026, MY26); GWM Cannon Alpha range page lists exactly two PHEV grades, Lux PHEV and Ultra PHEV, with Build & Price at https://www.gwmanz.com/au/config/cannon-alpha/ (script-rendered, prices not readable). CarExpert 2026 price list (24 Aug 2026) agrees on two PHEV grades.

listPrice.note: CarExpert 2026 listing: 'prices starting at $54,990' before on-road costs; CarsGuide 2026 price page gives the same MSRP ($54,990). GWM itself publishes only drive-away: $57,490 VIC private on gwmanz offers page (base price; the 'additional $3,000 off' to 30 Nov 2026 is a campaign, ignored). Verification: driveAwayPrice(listPrice 54990, isNonPassenger true) = 57354.73, within $135 of GWM's $57,490, so the MSRP agrees with the manufacturer's drive-away; a ute-divisor back-out would give 55122. Taken as the manufacturer's own RRP. Held price was 59,990 (2025 launch list), now lower.

batteryKwh.note: GWM AU: '37.1kWh of usable battery capacity'; CarExpert 2026 spec: 'Maximum battery kilowatt hour: 37.11 kWh'. Usable per GWM's own wording.

rangeKm.note: GWM AU 'Up to 115km of pure electric range', GWM internal testing; CarExpert states 115km NEDC. No WLTP exists: GWM sells this ute only in non-WLTP markets (AU, NZ, China); checked GWM AU and NZ pages. Testers: Chasing Cars 115km indicated mixed, CarExpert about 85km highway-heavy.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 37.11 / 115 x 100 = 32.27; no published EV-mode figure. Tautological against the cross-check.

combinedRangeKm.note: rangeKm + tank / fuelConsumptionL100km x 100 = 115 + 75 / 8.4 x 100 = 1008. Tank 75L per CarExpert 2026 spec. GWM's own figure is 1,060km 'nedc range (combined)' (powertrains page).

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: GWM charge-sustaining convention, ordered by mass across its Hi4-T PHEVs per dispatcher instruction (heavier car, higher fuel use): gwm-cannon-phev 8.1 (2585kg), gwm-tank-300-phev 8.3, gwm-tank-500-phev 8.4; Cannon Alpha is 2810kg (CarExpert), so set at 8.4. GWM's own numbers would give 7.9: CarExpert 2026 Ultra spec lists a secondary petrol figure of 7.9 L/100km, and GWM's 1,060km NEDC combined range gives (1060-115)/75 = 7.94 L/100km, which would put the heavier Alpha below the lighter Cannon's 8.1 derived the same way. Real-world: Chasing Cars just over 10 L/100km in hybrid mode; CarExpert 6.6 and CarsGuide 6.2-6.4 with charging mixed in.

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: Combined label 1.7 L/100km (ADR 81/02), at or below 3.5.

isGreenForVicDuty.note: Ute: field rules require false on every ute row; Victoria charges utes as goods vehicles (isNonPassengerForVicDuty true).

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Tub litres unpublished. CarExpert 2026 spec: tray length 1500mm, width 1520mm, height 500mm (1100mm between wheelhouses). 1500 x 1520 x 500 = 1140 L; reads 10-20% high because arches are ignored and the spare stands in the tub. Siblings: Cannon PHEV 1196, Shark 6 1200, Ranger PHEV 1185.

towKg.note: Braked towing 3,500 kg; GWM powertrains page 'towing capacity 3,500 KG'.

warrantyYears.note: Whole vehicle 84 months, unlimited km; battery 96 months. GWM page '7-year unlimited kilometre warranty', no servicing condition.

insuranceAnnual.note: Anchored to gwm-tank-300-phev-lux (1850 at $55,990), byd-shark-6-premium (1800 at $57,900) and ford-ranger-phev-xl (1700 at $56,592); above gwm-cannon-phev-lux (1700 at $48,793). Lowered from 1900 with the lower list price.

depreciationCurve.note: GWM ute convention, same curve as gwm-cannon-phev (refreshed 2026-11-26). Evidence for below-mainstream retention: repeated drive-away campaigns ($57,490 Lux drive-away was a 2025 campaign price that became standard; a further $3,000 off ran to 30 Nov 2026 per gwmanz offers). Note other GWM families hold different curves (Tank 300 0.71, Tank 500 0.67, Haval H6 0.71).

gwm-cannon-alpha-phev-lux.bootLitresSeatsUp: tub volume multiplied out from dimensions, reads high (same for Ultra and SeatsDown)
gwm-cannon-alpha-phev-lux.insuranceAnnual: judged against Tank 300, Shark 6 and Ranger PHEV
